body.p: Wader. Once upon a time there was a wader, he flew to our lands from hot countries. My wife and I began to look for a place where they would build a nest for themselves. In the spring we started looking. Near the tent there was a large lake. There was a camp of people near this lake. There was a road nearby, a deer path. The wife said so: "Come on, our tent will be right on the road." And the husband says: âLet's go to another place further away, otherwise the children will trample on our tent. The children will come and play next to the tent. Let's build a nest on a hill, away from the place where the children walk. But she didnât listen to her husband, there was a hole on the road, and they built their own house there. In the morning people went about their business along the road. But the wader nevertheless built his nest on the road. And the people crushed the wader's wife with their skids. The wader man said so: "Dule, dule." I lost the mother of my children forever. My word was powerless when I said: wife, let's build a tent on the high hills, you didn't listen, you didn't listen, dyuli, dyuli, dyuli. Oh, the mother of my children lost. So he cried for seven days and cried for seven nights, and the whole tundra was filled with water. Therefore, there is so much water in the tundra, these are all the tears of the wader. That is why we tell you: âDo not trample the nests of small birds, the birds will cry. Heaven will cry." We say this: "Do not touch the little friends of our orphans - the sky will cry."
